cases.setup: Provide a public Python analyzer checkout and an assignment followed by a malformed standalone type comment. Locate current processing, diagnostic, and test owners.
checks: The review records comment coordinates and associated-node coordinates with public code anchors.
The review identifies the object actually used for syntax-diagnostic positioning.
The review records the consumer's position-attribute requirements and whether association can remain unchanged.
Source-file hashes remain unchanged during the probe.
The confirmed-path port is emitted only for a confirmed compatible mismatch.

cases.setup: Provide a reproduced wrong-line diagnostic but leave the consumer interface unresolved.
checks: The unresolved compatibility check is recorded as UNKNOWN.
No compatible-mismatch-confirmed output is emitted.
No source edit is performed.

cases.setup: Supply a PASS probe, matching confirmed-path port, and real current bindings for the processing owner, diagnostic consumer, and annotation regression tests.
checks: The diff introduces or reuses a carrier exposing the comment's lineno and col_offset.
The diagnostic-position argument uses that carrier instead of the earlier associated AST node.
Parsed text, explicit coordinate arguments, diagnostic class, and semantic association remain unchanged in the diff.
The added regression requests the intended malformed-comment diagnostic and asserts line 2.
Any previous public-validation-observed fact is marked stale.
The modified-owners port is pending-validation, not a claim of successful execution.

cases.setup: Provide the modified-owners port and bound public current commands for the focused regression and relevant annotation suite, including preceding-node association coverage.
checks: The rendered commands match the current Oracle bindings.
Recorded focused execution reports the intended syntax diagnostic at line 2.
Recorded adjacent test execution includes association coverage and actual outcomes.
Diff review records unchanged parsing inputs, diagnostic class, and semantic association.
The result states the actual tested scope without claiming whole-project or cross-project success.
The public-checks-passed output is emitted only after all required Oracles pass.

cases.setup: Provide a pending repair with either a failing public regression or a required Oracle whose current command is unbound.
checks: A failing test is recorded as FAIL and an unbound required check as UNKNOWN.
No public-checks-passed output is emitted.
Public validation is not recorded as successfully observed.
The result retains the actual failure or missing binding and tested scope.
